constitution_acknowledgment: I am an untrusted implementation agent. I will not optimize for green gates.
scientific_question: Can a patient-specific counterfactual model predict which shunt intervention produces the best outcome?
the_2029_vision: Transform shunt management from reactive trial-and-error to proactive simulation-guided decision-making. Instead of 'adjust valve → wait → see', the clinician simulates 5 interventions, ranks by predicted outcome, and chooses the best.

experiment_design.method: RF Regressor predicts outcome score from patient features + intervention. Recommend intervention with lowest predicted score. Compare vs random (trial-and-error) and optimal.
experiment_design.outcome_metric: composite score: |mean_ICP - target| + overdrainage_penalty + underdrainage_penalty + variability_penalty

results.question: Can a patient-specific counterfactual model predict which shunt intervention produces the best outcome?
results.method: Random Forest Regressor, 5-fold CV. Patient features → predicted outcome score for each intervention → recommend best.

outcome_prediction.interpretation: The model predicts intervention outcome scores with R²=0.863 (explains 86.3% of variance)

results.win_threshold: recommendation accuracy > 50% AND improvement over random > 20%
results.key_finding: Counterfactual engine picks the right intervention 53.3% of the time (chance=20%), improving outcomes by 14.4% over trial-and-error.
results.candidate_state_change: NONE — light simulation. But result determines whether D4 advances to full pre-registered experiment.

attacks.attack: The outcome model is synthetic — real patient outcomes are messier and harder to predict.
attacks.countermeasure: First-order simulation. Real validation is Level 7.

attacks.attack: The model is trained and tested on the same data (no train/test split for recommendation evaluation).
attacks.countermeasure: The outcome R² uses 5-fold CV. The recommendation accuracy uses a model trained on ALL data (in-practice deployment). A proper train/test split for recommendation would be more rigorous.

attacks.attack: The 5 interventions are simplified — real interventions are more complex (specific valve models, catheter types, surgical approaches).
attacks.countermeasure: The 5 interventions represent the major decision classes. Real implementation would have more.

uncertainty_ledger_update.next_discriminator: If WIN: full pre-registered experiment (Article XXXVI) + independent reproduction + Gate 2 deep obviousness search. If KILL: generate new hypotheses.
